prize_parts.citation: For the development of palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, making the construction of aryl amines a general and practical synthetic operation

statement.case_for: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is the clearest case on the shortlist of a chemical idea that changed how molecules are made. Ligand design (bulky, electron-rich phosphines and biaryl phosphines) took C-N bond formation from a harsh, substrate-limited problem to a routine reaction, with a mechanism worked out in detail (oxidative addition, amine binding, reductive elimination). More than 25 years of independent confirmation, textbook status and routine use in medicinal and process chemistry can be checked in the literature and in industry. Attribution is clean: two laureates, with Kosugi's tin-amide coupling a precursor rather than the general catalytic method. The discovery was made in chemistry, by chemists, and I can say exactly what was new chemically.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki): some will say C-N coupling is an extension of an already honoured concept, and that the Academy has rewarded this territory. A second concern is that opening support was thin (only my own ballot), so I must show that scientific merit holds when the other members' arguments are weighed rather than assume it. A third is that Kosugi's precursor and the strongly competing candidates with larger therapeutic reach (degraders, lipid nanoparticles, base editing) may seem more consequential to a broader audience.

responses.point: Photoredox catalysis (B064) is a general, mild way to use single-electron transfer in synthesis, widely used in pharma and now mature after more than fifteen years.
responses.response: I agree on the science and ranked it third. It is my closest alternative, since it is also a broadly adopted methodology. My reservations are credit and fit: the field began from several near-simultaneous reports (MacMillan, Yoon, Stephenson, with Fukuzumi, Konig, Nicewicz and Melchiorre close behind), MacMillan was honoured in 2021 for organocatalysis, and a prize for Yoon and Stephenson alone would be defensible but contentious. Buchwald and Hartwig have much cleaner attribution, and I would put the allocation problem ahead of any claim that the photoredox concept is less important.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B044) introduced a new small-molecule modality built on induced proximity, with Crews and Deshaies as PROTAC originators and Handa's cereblon work explaining the molecular glue branch.
responses.response: The concept is original and the bifunctional-molecule design is chemically interesting, and I take it seriously as an alternative. What gives me pause is that the prize would honour two distinct strands (PROTACs and cereblon glues) with eight credited names and a three-person cap, and no PROTAC has yet been approved, as several colleagues note. I would also ask what was new chemically as opposed to chemical biology: the cereblon discovery is a target identification result. I would not call it premature, but the attribution and clinical record are less settled than for C-N coupling.

responses.point: Base editing (B019) is an explicit deaminase chemistry on a Cas-bound single-stranded DNA window that gives single-nucleotide change without double-strand breaks, and the prize would conventionally credit Liu.
responses.response: Liu's contribution is real and the tool is used everywhere. My concern is the border: the enabling concept is Cas9 targeting, honoured in 2020, and the chemical novelty is the fusion and evolution of deaminases to act in that window. That strikes me as a protein engineering advance on an already-rewarded platform, and the independent Kondo and Nishida work complicates priority. A Liu-only prize also leaves open whether prime editing should travel with it. I would rank it below C-N coupling, but I do not claim it is weak.

responses.point: Halide perovskite solar absorbers (B014) took efficiencies from a few percent to above 25 percent in about a decade, and nanopore sequencing (B068) turned a physical principle into a general analytical capability.
responses.response: I see the perovskite efficiency record as striking but agree with the stability and lead-toxicity caveats you list, and with the six-name credit problem; it is a chain of steps rather than a single molecule-level idea, and Sparr and Zou also place it lower. Nanopore sequencing is mature and impressive, but a chemistry citation would have to explain what is new chemically, as opposed to physics and biotechnology. I would want the committee to be as demanding of those candidates as of mine.

uncertainties: Whether a majority sees C-N coupling as meaningfully distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize or as overlapping it.
How much weight Kosugi's precursor work deserves in the citation and attribution record, and whether it changes the laureate pair.
Whether a prize for photoredox catalysis can be framed fairly given MacMillan's 2021 award and the crowded early credit.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My Masamune background is in stereocontrolled synthesis and I have no stated personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig or other shortlisted candidates; I share a Lund affiliation with Linke and Sparr, but this is not a conflict for any shortlisted candidate.
